# Building a planetarynervous system

Atmospheric data is the biggest missing piece to improving modern forecasts. We fuse data from our long-duration balloons with state-of-the-art AI models to produce the most accurate weather forecasts.

## Our end-to-end system

1. ### 01Observe




Harness Atlas, our global constellation of long-duration atmospheric balloons. Access critical data around the planet, including over oceans and the world’s most remote places.

    [Explore our constellation](https://windbornesystems.com/platform/observations)

2. ### 02Predict




Deploy WeatherMesh, our deep learning forecast model utilizing our proprietary data. Leverage forecasts that surpass the accuracy of other physics and AI-based models.

    [Explore our models](https://windbornesystems.com/platform/forecasts)

3. ### 03Act




Make the weather work for you. Transform forecast data into actionable insights and automations tailored to your needs.

    [Explore solutions](https://windbornesystems.com/weather-by-windborne)

## Complete global access, from surface to stratosphere

WindBorne designs, builds, and operates the only technology that captures atmospheric profiles everywhere. Each [balloon](https://windbornesystems.com/platform/observations) controls its altitude and flies autonomously for weeks.

**Traditional weather balloon** One vertical profile.Short lifetime of around 2 hours.

**WindBorne Global Sounding Balloon (GSB)** Around 50 controlled vertical profiles per GSB.Multi-week lifetime and targeted global reach.

18KM12KM6KMLAUNCHDAY 5DAY 10DAY 15DAY 20DAY 25DAY 30DAY 35

The solid flight trace shows repeated descents through the troposphere over more than 35 days, with cruising altitude rising from around 11 to 18 kilometers. The dashed trace shows a traditional balloon’s single ascent.

Flight W-2684, launched April 10, 2025, illustrates both tropospheric and stratospheric soundings.

## Our unparalleled atmospheric constellation

Atlas is the largest balloon constellation in the world and the foundation of our planetary nervous system. We launch hundreds of autonomous, next-generation weather balloons each month and are scaling Atlas to permanently close atmospheric data gaps from pole to pole.
